correctness.rationale: All essential computations were independently replayed and all boundary proofs checked. Cycle counts 7 (n=4), 14/15 (n=6), 22/26/28/28/29 (n=8), 57 (Petersen), 213 (Heawood), 170 (7-prism) were reproduced exactly by an independent edge-subset degree-2+connectedness enumerator (2^m subsets) for m<=15 and by an independent DFS enumerator for m=21. Optima L=8, 12/12, 16x5, 21, 28/28 were reproduced exactly by an independent Dijkstra-over-masks solver with no first-edge heuristic. Every listed cover was checked to consist of genuine simple cycles covering all m edges with total == L. Census completeness was reproduced: labeled enumeration with N(0) fixed gives 1/7/553 labeled and 1/7/552 connected (553-552=1 is exactly K4+K4, the only possible disconnected case), class counts 1/2/5 via explicit iso search; pairwise brute-force permutation check (40320 perms) confirms the five n=8 reps are pairwise non-isomorphic; all 11 graphs verified cubic, connected, bridgeless. Bridge-side lemma proof is valid: bridge side with k vertices has (3k-1)/2 internal edges so k odd; k=1 gives degree-1, k=3 needs 4>3 edges, so k>=5 each side and n>=10, hence no bridged connected cubic at n<=8. 7m/5 audit arithmetic correct (Petersen 21=21 tight; others 8<=8.4, 12<=12.6, 16<=16.8, 28<=29.4). R*=1.4 at Petersen correct. Limitations honestly stated (full n=14 stratum NOT claimed). Optima are exhaustive-search certificates (Dijkstra/B&B/IDA* logs), not human-readable proofs, but they are deterministic and replayed. Minor presentation defect: DRAFT says 'all four bridgeless classes' at n=8 where five are meant and certified; does not affect any computation.

originality.rationale: Strongest headline (Petersen L=21 = 7m/5 tight witness) is substantively anticipated. Hagglund-Markstrom arXiv:1306.3088 Sec.1 states that Brinkmann et al. [BGHM13] generated all snarks to n<=36 and computed scc(G), finding only two with scc=4m/3+1 — the Petersen graph and a 34-vertex snark — all others 4m/3. For Petersen m=15, 4m/3+1=21=7m/5. This is an explicit prior publication of the exact headline value and its tightness meaning, not a different invariant. Existence/upper-bound theory does not merely bound it: the prior is an exact-minimum computation of the same invariant on the same graph. The remaining n<=8 + Heawood values L=4m/3 are mechanically implied without search: universal cubic lower bound L>=4m/3 (each vertex needs >=2 cycle incidences, so L=sum t_v >=2n=4m/3) plus the textbook upper bound 'if G is 3-edge-colourable then scc=4m/3 by taking two pairs of colours' (stated as easy in the same prior, Thm 5.4: tau<=4 => scc=4m/3). All n<=8 cubics are Class 1 by the classical smallest-snark-is-Petersen fact; Heawood is bipartite hence 3-edge-colourable by Konig. So those table entries require only exhibiting a 4m/3 cover, no new optimization. 7-prism value 28=4m/3 is likewise a lower-bound-tight cover, not a new tightness phenomenon. No source tabulating per-graph minima for the full n=14 stratum was found, but the delivered headline is not that census — it is the Petersen tight witness plus small 4m/3 cases — and the former is prior. A timestamp or failed search does not establish priority; substantive comparison shows definitional anticipation. Hence FAIL, which is never repairable.

value.rationale: Judging the strongest self-contained delivered headline separately from the unfinished n=14 survey: the Petersen exact value L=21 with explicit minimum cover attaining the Alon-Tarsi bound 7m/5 is an independently retrievable exact invariant of a specific natural object. Object (Petersen, canonical smallest snark) and invariant (shortest cycle cover length, testing 7m/5 tightness within CDC/Fulkerson/Petersen-colouring programs) were motivated before computation (Kaiser et al. abstract confirms 7m/5 as recognized conjecture); the value is not mechanically implied for a snark (requires solving the optimum; lower bound >20 needs proof); a future researcher could reasonably need the precise witness, cover, and tightness bit for benchmarking. This meets the narrow-datum eligibility: one exact constant/witness can be worth retrieving without a new general theorem. The incomplete n=14 census is honestly disclaimed (only Heawood + 7-prism exhibits) and cannot be called complete, but it does not erase the headline witness value. The n<=8 4m/3 sub-table alone would be a textbook restatement and would fail value, but the Petersen tightness extremal carries independent value. Hence PASS on the headline.

decisive_checks: Re-ran inputs/artifacts/run.py: reproduced labeled 1/7/553, connected 1/7/552, classes 1/2/5, L values 8,12,12,16x5,21,28,28 and R*=1.4 at Petersen.

Independent edge-subset cycle enumerator (degree==2 + connected + |V|==|E| over all 2^m subsets) matched claimed ncycles_total 7,14,15,28,26,22,29,28,57 for all m<=15 graphs; independent DFS enumerator matched 213 (Heawood) and 170 (prismY7).
Independent Dijkstra-over-masks (branching over all cycles, no first-edge restriction) matched all 11 optima; all listed verts sequences verified as simple cycles covering every edge with total == L.

Brute-force permutation iso check (8!=40320) confirmed five n=8 reps pairwise non-isomorphic; all 11 graphs verified cubic/connected/bridgeless; bridge-side lemma algebra verified (k odd, k=1/3 impossible, so k>=5, n>=10).

Lower-bound proof L>=4m/3 for cubic covers verified (t_v>=2 per vertex); combined with prior '3-edge-colourable => scc=4m/3' this makes n<=8/Heawood entries mechanically implied; prior 1306.3088 Sec.1 verified to publish scc(Petersen)=4m/3+1=21.
residual_risks: DRAFT typo 'all four bridgeless classes' at n=8 (should be five); no effect on artifacts but requires copy-edit if ever reused.
Optimality evidence is exhaustive-search logs (states/nodes), not human-checkable case analysis; replay depends on stdlib Python determinism, verified here but not formally proved correct in prose.

7-prism edge-chromatic status (odd prism Class 2 vs tau=4) was not needed for correctness since optimum was brute-forced, but any claim that its 4m/3 value follows from 3-edge-colourability alone would be inaccurate; value rests on explicit cover + UNSAT log, not on colourability.
Full n=14 stratum (up to 509 graphs) remains open; draft honestly disclaims it, so no completeness misrepresentation, but R* over 11 graphs must not be mistaken for stratum R*.
